name: Binnui
overview: The topic of Binnui in Scripture highlights several individuals connected to the Jewish captivity and restoration period, emphasizing their roles within the community and temple service. Binnui, also known as Bani, appears as a leader of a significant family group with over six hundred members (Ezra 2:10; Nehemiah 7:15), indicating his importance among the exiles. He is identified as a Levite and the father of Noadiah, who served in the house of God (Ezra 8:33), and as a descendant of Pahath-moab, showing his tribal lineage (Ezra 10:30). Additionally, Binnui is noted for his active participation in the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s walls, symbolizing faithful service during the restoration (Nehemiah 3:24). These references collectively present Binnui as a faithful servant of God, integral to the community's identity and worship after captivity.
